transcript: I can spot a vibe-coded website in three seconds. Big fancy fonts, cream and beige backgrounds, orange buttons, and generic UI. If you don't want your websites to look like this, I'm a software engineer and a data scientist who vibe codes all the time. Level one: start with references. Go to sites like Land-book or Godly design for inspiration. Find a few designs you like, screenshot them, and upload them to a vibe coding tool. Level two: get super specific with your prompts. Don't just say make it look clean like Apple. Describe the layout, the colors, the spacing, and what you want to avoid. Level three: set your design rules. Create one master prompt with your fonts, colors, spacings, and button styles. Then reuse it so every page feels like the part of same website. Level four: design the layout. Build your custom design by prompting in Replit Design or simply by choosing from a list of templates. Then turn those designs into a fully functional website with a simple prompt. So save this reel before you start your next project.
